localBiteReport: This week's conditions on Choctawhatchee Bay are recovering from Hurricane Isaias (which made landfall near Destin on October 9), but the bay never muddied up severely — guide Capt. Blake Nelson of Last Cast Charters reports it took on a tannin-stained tint rather than heavy silt, and the Destin flats have retained enough visibility for sight fishing. Redfish remain the top inshore target: smaller slot fish (around 23 inches and under) are holding on familiar guts, potholes, and shallow-water feeding areas across the bay flats, while larger overslot reds are transitioning to a more mobile fall pattern and showing up around bridges at night. A guide reporting from the Fort Walton Beach/Destin area on captainexperiences.com (approximately two weeks ago) noted that redfish and trout are heating up in the bayous as part of the fall transition during the Destin Fishing Rodeo. Water temperature at this location is 76°F. Blake Nelson expects each successive fall cold front to improve the artificial-lure bite on the flats, with the classic winter creek-and-river-mouth pattern for trout still weeks away — closer to January.
